answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task can a slash occur. This approach is like navigating an ocean of deceit, where only the strongest identities can prevail. A well-crafted anti-Sybil mechanism is like a sonnet, with precise language and structure, cutting through the noise. Just as a marble is polished to perfection, a robust anti-Sybil system refines its defenses, ensuring only legitimate identities can participate.
